about: A small set of real first-person texts of the kinds a founder, an aggrieved or a bereaved person writes, as a tone reference for the composing model's pieces (docs/behaviour/founding.md, 'Softening'; cited in docs/research/references.md). Each was opened on 2026-10-11 and its excerpt copied as the page had it. Used only to be measured (word counts and the rubric); never shown to a model as an example, never training data. Limits: ten texts, all in English, from three countries; petitions and inquiry submissions are written to an authority, which a founder's statement to neighbours is not; nothing was found for a redundancy, and one thin text for an eviction. Licences are as the sites state them; where a site's licence does not cover third-party content the entry says unclear.

texts.source: UK Parliament petition 728581, 'Give maternity leave to those who've suffered baby loss from 20 weeks gestation'
texts.text: I wish for the government to grant maternity leave after baby loss form 20 weeks gestation. I think this should be an option for those who still need time to heal, as 2 weeks bereavement after losing your child is not only too little for a physical recovery but for mental recovery too. I have recently suffered baby loss at 20 weeks and 5 days due to PPROM and Anhydramnios. Under current law, our loss comes under miscarriage. I had to give birth to our child and make the decision to terminate or let him die inside my body. This to me and many others is not a miscarriage. I have also suffered a miscarriage at 5 weeks and 5 days, there is a huge difference between the two. I believe maternity leave would have given me and everyone else this is happening to, the chance to start to heal.

texts.source: UK Parliament petition 759136, 'Change your definition of carers allowance to "carers supplement"'
texts.text: I want carers allowance to be put in a different bracket from a "base benefit". I believe it keeps carers in poverty because currently you cannot get two base benefits at once. State pension & bereavement allowance are also base benefits.Right now, carers allowance is removed if you claim either. I am coming up to pensionable age. I learnt, when I apply for my pension, my carers allowance will be removed! I will still be looking after my son for the 133 hrs I currently do, so why/how can it be right to remove this. When my husband died, my carers allowance was removed because I claimed bereavement allowance for the following year even though I was still looking after my son. How is this fair/right? Please recognise the work we carers do and the money we save the government. Value us!

texts.kind: a refused claim, after a death
texts.source: UK Parliament petition 778376, 'Review Funeral Expenses Payment rules for people in full-time work'
texts.text: I want the Government to review Funeral Expenses Payment eligibility so that people like me, who work full-time but cannot afford an unexpected funeral, can receive support based on their actual financial circumstances rather than being excluded because they do not receive a qualifying benefit. I was refused Funeral Expenses Payment because I work full-time and do not receive a qualifying benefit, despite being unable to afford my father's unexpected funeral due to limited savings, a mortgage and bills. I believe the rules unfairly assume that being employed means people can afford these costs and should consider income and financial circumstances rather than receipt of benefits.

texts.source: UK Parliament petition 732563, 'Review how mobility side of PIP is assessed for those that can drive'
texts.text: I would like government to review how the mobility side of PIP is assessed for those that can drive. Some disabled people who drive are being refused this lifeline due to being able to "plan and carry out a journey" etc. I think this is extremely unfair and needs to be changed. I am disabled. I am partially paralyzed on my left side and have just been denied the mobility side of PIP because I can drive my car which is automatic. I do not use my left side to drive and so don't need to grip anything with my left hand. I have read about lots of other people being refused the mobility side because they can drive and plan journeys etc. I feel we are being denied our independence for which PIP was intended.

texts.source: UK Parliament petition 709248, 'Ask Bath & North East Somerset Council to provide Wheelchair Accessible Taxis'
texts.text: I am an adult wheelchair user. The list of wheelchair accessible taxis (WAV) on the council website is misleading. Only one operates in Bath and often tied up with school runs. This is an essential service to the disabled community. I've been left in the rain by regular taxis who refused to take me. I am currently applying for a WAV with Motabilty Foundation and in discussing my needs I have explained how frustrating it is to access a local WAV taxi. They have told me this is a nationwide problem. The Equality Act 2010 is meant to level up access to enable disabled people to be as independent as possible and have good quality of life as does the rest of the population.

texts.kind: an eviction after a debt was taken
texts.source: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme, anonymous submission ANO.9999.0001.0094
texts.licence: unclear (the site is CC BY 4.0 except content supplied by third parties, which a submission is)
texts.text: To whom it may concern,I am a tier 2 robodebt victim. I am also a victim of fraud and misuse of power by services Australia. But to get straight to the point, I received the pathetic compensation for being threatened and bullied, about 71$. Ive disputed and appealed this but prior to Xmas I had a Aat level 2 hearing regarding my debt. Ten days prior to the Aat 2 hearing and AFTER Robodebt compensation was paid, Centrelink removed another 5000$ from my debt and then recalculated payments without telling me. This resulted in me being evicted after a large repayment was taken from my account. Bottom line. that extra 5000$ should have been included in Robodebt calculations. I contacted Services Australia and was screamed at. The next step is a notice of claim. Now I can tell the judge I've exhausted all avenues. Thankyou

texts.kind: a disputed debt for support paid
texts.source: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme, anonymous submission ANO.9999.0001.0036
texts.licence: unclear (third-party content on a CC BY 4.0 site)
texts.text: I received a Centrelink letter regarding under-reporting of income after the end of the 2016 / 2017 financial year. The claimed discrepancy was $2,000+ resulting in overpayment of approximately $800 in benefits. When I received the letter, I was unphased because I knew I had not under-reported income. I was diligent about reporting fortnightly on the specified date and was mindful of reporting net rather than gross income. On report dates, I had not yet received pay slips so calculated income based on work rosters and hourly rate. Nevertheless, I realised Centrelink would require evidence. Unfortunately, I had not retained all relevant paperwork. I had not kept a record of reported hours / income and had deleted emailed rosters and payslips over 12 months old. However, through group certificates and bank statements I established immediately the disputed amount corresponded to the lapse between the hours I worked in May / June 2016 and their payment in July 2016. Adjusting for those factors, the discrepancy was less than $80 not $2,000+.

texts.kind: a disputed debt, a death, a mother writing for her daughter
texts.source: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme, anonymous submission ANO.9999.0001.0116 (its last paragraph)
texts.licence: unclear (third-party content on a CC BY 4.0 site)
texts.text: My daughter and my family are hard working TAX paying Citizens of this Country. We do not break the law we are community minded and love our life and country. To be treated so bad from our Government. That we pay so much tax to. Is a disgrace. This all got so bad for us. My daughter R had to give up. Her health was suffering. This was killing me to see her like this. Hence I have taken over. I will not stop, for her. She is a hair dresser, minimum wage. Infact her earnings are very low. She wanted to better herself and went part time work and then started to study at UNI an arts degree. Centrelink Debt made her to feel unworthy, untrusting, like she is a criminal trying to dodge paying. Honestly this is how we felt. ALSO then, the good old Covid hit, No income for her. She got pregnant and had a miscarriage. Her beautiful young Father died suddenly. All within a 2 year period and still having Centrelink over her head.

texts.kind: why a tenants' union was started (an organiser, looking back)
texts.source: Tracy Jeanne Rosenthal, '101 Notes on the LA Tenants Union', Commune, 2019 (as reposted by The Anarchist Library)
texts.text: We started LATU in 2015, with a single meeting in Hollywood. We have since expanded to ten local chapters, which meet twice a month across the city, and have now organized dozens of tenants' associations, some with hundreds of members. LATU is a member-funded union. We are not a non-profit. We receive no funding except from dues, which average five dollars a month. We are an all-volunteer effort. This is how we got started: In 2012, School of Echoes, a group of people, diverse in age, race, and organizing experience, figured out that what we all had in common was living in neighborhoods undergoing a process often euphemized as "change."

texts.kind: why a mutual-aid network was started (a coordinator, quoted by a journalist)
texts.source: The Ecologist, 'The birth of Covid-19 mutual aid', 16 March 2020 (Anna Vickerstaff, quoted)
texts.text: No matter what we look like, where we live, or how much money we have, getting sick reminds us that at our core we're all just human. And in every country it's the old, the sick and those already struggling who will be affected worse. That's why we set this network up - because we want to make sure that no one in our communities is being left to face this crisis alone, and because we want to try and redress some of the serious inequalities this outbreak will expose. Groups are being set up and run entirely by volunteers - and our hope is that they can help to make sure people who need support get it.
